alt_text: Photo in Eixample, Barcelona. Text on the image: Show, don't tell: three swaps
caption:
Labels like nervous, cold and tired tell the reader what to feel. A detail lets them notice it for themselves. Three swaps to try:
"She was nervous" → her fingers tapped the table.
"It was cold" → breath fogged the glass.
"He was tired" → he read the same line twice. The method is simple: pick one detail the senses can check. Could someone see it, hear it or touch it? If so, it will usually do more than the adjective. The same habit helps outside fiction. In a report, an email or a presentation, a concrete detail is often clearer than a general claim. Try it on one sentence you wrote today.
